title: PatternBoost Alternates Local Search & Transformers to Disprove a 30-Year-Old Hypercube Conjecture
aiSystem: PatternBoost (Makemore Transformer + Local Search — Meta FAIR / UW–Madison / DeepMind / Sydney)
whyItMatters: Alternating fast local search with lightweight transformer training autonomously disproved a 30-year-old conjecture on spanning subgraphs of the 6-dimensional hypercube and broke multiple extremal combinatorics records.
summary: Published in November 2024 (arXiv:2411.00566) by François Charton (Meta FAIR), Jordan S. Ellenberg (UW–Madison), Adam Zsolt Wagner (Google DeepMind), and Geordie Williamson (University of Sydney), PatternBoost introduced a general two-phase 'local–global' discovery loop for extremal mathematics: a fast local heuristic constructs high-scoring combinatorial objects, and a small transformer is iteratively trained on the top discoveries to learn global structural patterns and sample improved seeds for the next local-search round. Applied to open problems across graph theory, geometry, and combinatorics, PatternBoost disproved a 30-year-old conjecture of Brouwer, Dejter, and Thomassen / Bondy on the minimum edges in a spanning subgraph of the 6-dimensional hypercube Q₆ containing no induced 4-cycle (constructing an explicit 81-edge counterexample beating the conjectured lower bound of 82) while also improving records on no-three-in-line, triangle-free graphs, and extremal set systems.
technicalHighlights: Alternates fast domain-specific local optimization with a compact transformer trained solely on the best discovered constructions—requiring no massive pretrained LLM.
Disproved a 30-year-old conjecture on induced C₄-free spanning subgraphs of the 6-cube Q₆ via an explicit, trivially checkable 81-edge construction (refuting the conjectured bound of 82).
Matched or surpassed best-known human extremal bounds across multiple benchmarks in discrete geometry and combinatorics.
caveats: Requires encoding candidate mathematical objects into compact token sequences and supplying a fast computable scoring function; excels at extremal constructions rather than deductive proofs.

scoreRationale.foundational: Demonstrated that tiny domain-trained transformers alternating with local search can crack decades-old extremal combinatorics conjectures.
scoreRationale.ripple: Adopted rapidly as a lightweight open-source discovery toolkit across combinatorics, knot theory, and discrete geometry.
scoreRationale.verification: Explicit 81-edge Q₆ hypercube counterexample and extremal constructions are deterministically verified by exact computation.
scoreRationale.velocity: Overturned a 30-year-old hypercube conjecture and improved multiple extremal bounds using lightweight local-search + transformer compute.
